newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korean leader hopes for bumper harvest.
newsitem.headline: North Korean leader hopes for bumper harvest.

text.p: North Korean leader Kim Jong-il on Tuesday thanked farmers, soldiers and other citizens for their work on the rice crop and urged them to keep striving to ensure an "unprecedented bumper harvest" this year.

"My thanks should be extended to the agricultural working people, People's Army soldiers and helpers for their great contributions to victoriously concluding this year's rice-transplanting," Kim Jong-il said in a statement.

"(They) should not rest content with their success but should engage themselves in weeding and proper manuring of crops and thus bring about an unprecedented bumper harvest this meaningful year," he said in the statement, carried by the official Korean Central News Agency monitored in Tokyo.
Severe floods destroyed food stocks and grain harvests in North Korea in 1995 and 1996, pushing the Stalinist state to the brink of famine.
Last week, a top United Nations official said North Korea was teetering on the edge of "a major humanitarian crisis" and needed outside help within weeks.
Peter McDermott, deputy director of emergency programmes at the United Nations Children's Fund, said after a trip to the North that all the signs of a crisis were in place.
